name: Gong Bingyan
about: I am Gong Bingyan, a Master of Cyber Security student at Universiti Malaya. My career focus is application security. I am interested in how software handles requests, permissions and data, and how developers can check that a repair works.

My background includes computing study, API and database projects, and an IT support internship. I have worked with Go, Python and Java and have used Linux and Docker in project work. These are foundations for learning, rather than a claim of professional AppSec experience.

In WQE7001, I am documenting an isolated Kali and Metasploitable lab and an Nmap service-discovery exercise. I use these projects to connect network observations with clear explanations and next steps. I want my portfolio to show evidence that others can inspect and reproduce. My next aim is to move from finding exposed services to testing, fixing and retesting weaknesses in my own applications.
career: My target is a junior application security or security testing role. I want to work with developers to understand a weakness, agree on a repair and check the result. My computing background gives me a starting point, but I still need stronger evidence of practical AppSec skills.

My next steps are to strengthen Linux and networking foundations, practise web/API authorization testing in an owned application, and document code repairs with repeatable tests. By February 2027, I aim to publish or improve a GitHub project that shows two issue, repair and retest cases, with setup instructions and clear results.

I will seek feedback on whether the work is correct and reproducible. GitHub stars can show interest, but tests, useful reviews and a verified repair will be my main quality checks. This is a development plan, not a claim that I already have professional AppSec experience.
